finding: The database connection has no read/write time limit. If the cloud database stalls on one request (connected but not answering), the app waits for ever. The 30-minute exit pass saves the book while it holds the mode lock, so one stuck save would freeze that pass; the next exit passes give up after 60 s thinking a rotation is running, and the next rotation waits for the lock with no limit. Stops and targets would then not be checked until the app restarts. The Den's database guard cannot help either: it measures a call only after the call returns. UNPROVEN that it has happened live; proven that nothing bounds it.
impact: EXIT - a single stalled database request can leave every open position without stop and target checks until a restart.
review_note: Fresh inspection: MongoClient explicitly sets connection/selection timeouts but no socket/operation timeout. URI options may alter runtime; actual live stall is unproven.
proposed_fix: Give the client a socket and operation time limit (e.g. socketTimeoutMS 20000 and timeoutMS 30000) so a stalled request fails and the existing error paths take over.
